text:
**I’d pick Monzo for most European trips**, assuming you’re comparing the free UK accounts. You can leave your money in pounds and pay by card at Mastercard’s exchange rate, with no Monzo fee, no monthly currency-exchange allowance to track and no weekend surcharge. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/travelling/understanding-fees?utm_source=openai))

**Revolut is the better fit if you want to buy euros ahead of time.** On Revolut Standard, you can exchange up to £1,000 per month on weekdays at Revolut’s rate without an extra fee. There’s a 1% fee on exchanges above that allowance and a 1% weekend exchange fee. The weekend fee is on *conversion*, not spending: if you’ve already bought enough euros on a weekday, paying in euros on Saturday won’t trigger it. ([help.revolut.com](https://help.revolut.com/help/profile-and-plan/my-plan-benefits/revolut-plans1/standard-plan/?utm_source=openai))

**If you’ll need cash**, Monzo also has the edge in the European Economic Area (the EU plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway). Its shared UK/EEA allowance is £400 every 30 days, or unlimited fee-free withdrawals if Monzo counts as your main bank. Outside the EEA, the free account allows £200 every 30 days. Revolut Standard allows £200 or five withdrawals per rolling month, whichever comes first. The ATM operator may charge its own fee. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/help/travelling/understanding-fees?utm_source=openai))

With either card, if the terminal offers **“GBP or local currency?” choose local currency** so the merchant doesn’t set the exchange rate. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/learn/money-abroad/things-to-know-pre-and-post-trip))
